result.builder:
Goal: add a new tool, jsonl-lint, as a workspace under packages/, and open one PR that meets every acceptance line of https://github.com/suredesigntshirts/ccp_machine_test/issues/102. Right now packages/ does not exist, the root package.json already declares workspaces ["packages/*"], and .github/workflows/test.yml runs `npm ci` then `npm test` on Node 22.

Acceptance lines (these are the pass/fail conditions):
1. packages/jsonl-lint/bin/jsonl-lint.js <file> prints <file>:<line>: <error> for every row that is not valid JSON (1-based lines, blank lines skipped, an unterminated last line checked) and exits 1 if any, 0 if none
2. A missing file or no argument prints to stderr and exits 2
3. packages/jsonl-lint/src/index.js exports lint(text) returning [{ line, error }]
4. The workspace has its own package.json (jsonl-lint, type module, test script node --test), no runtime dependencies, and node:test tests for a clean file, a bad middle row, a torn last row, blank lines and the exit codes
5. packages/jsonl-lint/README.md exists and the root README lists the tool
6. The change is one PR on suredesigntshirts/ccp_machine_test whose body says Closes https://github.com/suredesigntshirts/ccp_machine_test/issues/102, and npm test and the test workflow are green at its head

Steps:
1. Create packages/jsonl-lint/package.json with "name": "jsonl-lint", "private": true, "type": "module", "bin": {"jsonl-lint": "bin/jsonl-lint.js"}, "scripts": {"test": "node --test"}, and NO "dependencies" field (no runtime dependencies at all). Plain ES modules, no build step, Node 22+.
2. Create packages/jsonl-lint/src/index.js exporting a named function `lint(text)`. Split the text on "\n" (strip a trailing "\r" from each row so CRLF files work). For each row, with 1-based line number = index + 1: skip it if it is blank (only whitespace); otherwise try JSON.parse; on failure push { line, error } where error is the parse error's message (a non-empty string). A final row without a trailing newline (a torn/unterminated last line) must be checked like any other row; a single trailing newline must not produce an extra row error. Return the array (empty when everything is valid). Keep it pure: no file or process access.
3. Create packages/jsonl-lint/bin/jsonl-lint.js with a `#!/usr/bin/env node` shebang (and make it executable, chmod +x). It takes one argument, a file path. If no argument is given, print a usage message to stderr and exit 2. If the file cannot be read (missing, etc.), print an error to stderr and exit 2. Otherwise read it as UTF-8, call lint, and for each result print to stdout exactly `<file>:<line>: <error>` where <file> is the argument exactly as given. Exit 1 if there was at least one error, 0 if none. Print nothing to stdout in the error-exit-2 cases. Use process.exitCode or exit after output is flushed.
4. Add node:test tests under packages/jsonl-lint/test/ (e.g. packages/jsonl-lint/test/lint.test.js) that `node --test` discovers from the workspace directory. Cover, each as its own named test: a clean file (lint returns [] and CLI exits 0 with no stdout); a bad middle row (reported with the correct 1-based line number, other rows not reported); a torn last row with no trailing newline (reported with its line number); blank lines (skipped, and they still count toward line numbers of later rows); and the exit codes 0, 1 and 2 by running the CLI with child_process (spawnSync of process.execPath on the bin file) against temp files (fs.mkdtempSync in os.tmpdir()), including the missing-file and no-argument cases exiting 2 with stderr output. Also check the CLI output format `<file>:<line>: <error>`.
5. Write packages/jsonl-lint/README.md: what the tool does, usage (`node packages/jsonl-lint/bin/jsonl-lint.js <file>`), output format, exit codes (0 clean, 1 invalid rows, 2 missing file / no argument), the `lint(text)` API returning [{ line, error }], and how to run the tests.
6. Update the root README.md: under "What is here", replace the "No tools yet" bullet with a bullet listing `packages/jsonl-lint` (the string jsonl-lint must appear) and a one-line description linking to its README.
7. Run `npm install` at the repo root so package-lock.json picks up the new workspace, and commit the updated package-lock.json; otherwise `npm ci` in the test workflow fails. Then run `npm ci && npm test` at the root and make sure it passes and actually runs the jsonl-lint tests.
8. Commit, push, and open exactly one PR on suredesigntshirts/ccp_machine_test whose body contains the line `Closes https://github.com/suredesigntshirts/ccp_machine_test/issues/102` and briefly summarises the change. Wait for the `test` workflow on the PR head and make sure it is green; if it fails, fix it and push to the same PR (don't open a second PR).
result.verifier:
Check the PR for https://github.com/suredesigntshirts/ccp_machine_test/issues/102 at its head commit. Run every command from the repository root of a checkout of the PR head, after `npm ci`. There is one check per acceptance line, in the same order. Each check quotes its line; PASS or FAIL depends only on that line.

Check 1 — "packages/jsonl-lint/bin/jsonl-lint.js <file> prints <file>:<line>: <error> for every row that is not valid JSON (1-based lines, blank lines skipped, an unterminated last line checked) and exits 1 if any, 0 if none"
Run:
d=$(mktemp -d) && printf '{"a":1}\n\n[1,2]\n"s"\n' > "$d/clean.jsonl" && printf '{"a":1}\n{bad\n\n{"b":2}\n{"c":' > "$d/bad.jsonl" && node packages/jsonl-lint/bin/jsonl-lint.js "$d/clean.jsonl" > "$d/o1" 2> "$d/e1"; echo "clean exit=$?"; cat "$d/o1"; node packages/jsonl-lint/bin/jsonl-lint.js "$d/bad.jsonl" > "$d/o2" 2> "$d/e2"; echo "bad exit=$?"; echo "file=$d/bad.jsonl"; cat "$d/o2"
The bad file has: line 1 valid, line 2 invalid (`{bad`), line 3 blank, line 4 valid, line 5 an unterminated invalid last row (`{"c":` with no newline).
PASS: `clean exit=0` and no stdout lines for the clean file; `bad exit=1`; stdout for the bad file is exactly two lines, the first starting with `<file>:2: ` and the second with `<file>:5: ` (<file> being the printed `file=` path), each followed by a non-empty error message; no line for 1, 3 or 4.
FAIL: any other exit code, a missing or extra line, wrong line numbers (e.g. 0-based, or blank lines not counted), the blank line reported, the torn last row not reported, or a format other than `<file>:<line>: <error>`.

Check 2 — "A missing file or no argument prints to stderr and exits 2"
Run:
node packages/jsonl-lint/bin/jsonl-lint.js /nonexistent/missing.jsonl > /tmp/jl-o 2> /tmp/jl-e; echo "missing exit=$?"; echo "stdout bytes=$(wc -c < /tmp/jl-o) stderr bytes=$(wc -c < /tmp/jl-e)"; node packages/jsonl-lint/bin/jsonl-lint.js > /tmp/jl-o 2> /tmp/jl-e; echo "noarg exit=$?"; echo "stdout bytes=$(wc -c < /tmp/jl-o) stderr bytes=$(wc -c < /tmp/jl-e)"
PASS: both `missing exit=2` and `noarg exit=2`, and stderr bytes > 0 in both cases.
FAIL: either exit code is not 2, or either case writes nothing to stderr.

Check 3 — "packages/jsonl-lint/src/index.js exports lint(text) returning [{ line, error }]"
Run:
node --input-type=module -e 'import { lint } from "./packages/jsonl-lint/src/index.js"; console.log(JSON.stringify(lint(["{\"a\":1}", "{bad", "", "{\"c\":"].join("\n")))); console.log(JSON.stringify(lint("{\"a\":1}\n\n[2]\n")));'
PASS: the import succeeds; the first printed line is an array of exactly two objects, each with a `line` and an `error` property, with line values 2 and 4 (in that order); the second printed line is `[]`.
FAIL: the import fails, `lint` is not a named export, the result is not an array of { line, error } objects, or the line values differ.

Check 4 — "The workspace has its own package.json (jsonl-lint, type module, test script node --test), no runtime dependencies, and node:test tests for a clean file, a bad middle row, a torn last row, blank lines and the exit codes"
Run:
node -e 'const p = JSON.parse(require("fs").readFileSync("packages/jsonl-lint/package.json", "utf8")); console.log(JSON.stringify({ name: p.name, type: p.type, test: p.scripts && p.scripts.test, dependencies: p.dependencies || null }))'; echo "exit=$?"
npm test -w packages/jsonl-lint; echo "exit=$?"
ls packages/jsonl-lint/test; grep -rn "test(\|it(\|describe(" packages/jsonl-lint/test
PASS: the first command prints name `jsonl-lint`, type `module`, a test script that runs `node --test`, and dependencies `null` or `{}`; `npm test -w packages/jsonl-lint` runs node:test tests and exits 0 with no failing tests; reading the test files (they import from `node:test`) shows tests covering each of: a clean file, a bad middle row, a torn (unterminated) last row, blank lines, and the CLI exit codes (the tests run the CLI and assert exit codes).
FAIL: package.json missing or any of name/type/test script wrong, any runtime dependency listed, the tests fail or are not node:test, or any of the five listed cases has no test.

Check 5 — "packages/jsonl-lint/README.md exists and the root README lists the tool"
Run:
test -f packages/jsonl-lint/README.md && echo "readme present" || echo "readme missing"; grep -n "jsonl-lint" README.md; echo "exit=$?"
PASS: `readme present`, and grep finds at least one line in the root README.md naming jsonl-lint as a tool (exit=0).
FAIL: `readme missing`, or the root README does not mention jsonl-lint.

Check 6 — "The change is one PR on suredesigntshirts/ccp_machine_test whose body says Closes https://github.com/suredesigntshirts/ccp_machine_test/issues/102, and npm test and the test workflow are green at its head"
Run (GraphQL is blocked in this environment, so use the REST API via gh api, not gh pr view):
gh api 'repos/suredesigntshirts/ccp_machine_test/pulls?state=all&per_page=100' --jq '.[] | select((.body // "") | contains("Closes https://github.com/suredesigntshirts/ccp_machine_test/issues/102")) | "\(.number) \(.state) \(.head.ref) \(.head.sha) \(.base.ref)"'; echo "exit=$?"
sha=$(gh api 'repos/suredesigntshirts/ccp_machine_test/pulls?state=all&per_page=100' --jq '.[] | select((.body // "") | contains("Closes https://github.com/suredesigntshirts/ccp_machine_test/issues/102")) | .head.sha' | head -n 1); echo "head=$sha"; gh api "repos/suredesigntshirts/ccp_machine_test/commits/$sha/check-runs" --jq '.check_runs[] | "\(.name) \(.status) \(.conclusion)"'; echo "exit=$?"
git rev-parse HEAD
npm ci && npm test; echo "exit=$?"
PASS: exactly one open (or merged) PR's body contains `Closes https://github.com/suredesigntshirts/ccp_machine_test/issues/102`; that PR contains the whole change; its head sha matches `git rev-parse HEAD` of the checkout you tested; the check run named `test` at that sha is `completed success`; and `npm ci && npm test` exits 0 locally, with the jsonl-lint tests among those run. If the workflow is still running, wait and re-run the check-runs command before deciding.
FAIL: no such PR, more than one PR for the change, the body lacks the exact Closes line, the `test` check run is missing, failing or cancelled at the head, or `npm ci && npm test` fails (e.g. package-lock.json not updated for the new workspace).

Advisory (not pass/fail conditions):
- Also try a CRLF file (printf '{"a":1}\r\n{bad\r\n' ) and a file ending in a single newline; noting stray errors on the trailing empty row or on \r is useful feedback.
- Check the bin file has a `#!/usr/bin/env node` shebang and that nothing is written to stdout in the exit-2 cases.
- A quick mutation (e.g. make lint skip the last row) should make the torn-row test fail; report if it does not.
